newsitem.title: INDIA: India metals ease, following world trends.
newsitem.headline: India metals ease, following world trends.

text.p: Tin and nickel prices eased, replicating world market trends, while other base metals showed a little more steadiness, traders said.
Supplies also improved as metals started flowing in from ports to markets following the end, last week, of a 10-day long truck strike.
Tin and nickel fell following fresh unloading by stockists in response to declines on world markets. Industrial buyers kept sidelines in the falling markets, traders said.
Tin fell by 200 rupees to 31,200 after losing 200 rupees on Saturday.
Nickel dropped 200 rupees to 36,300 per quintal after losing 300 rupees on Saturday.
Other metals were steady but undercurrent was weak amid sluggish industrial buying as well as falling global prices.
Copper was quiet at 13,525 rupees, as was zinc at 7,850 rupees and lead at 4,550 rupees.
Volume was slow as major players kept sidelines awaiting announcement of the selling prices by state-owned agencies for the second half of the current month.
